prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
There isn’t a single “official” service that tells you whether ChatGPT (or other LLMs) will recommend your business. The best practical approach is a mix of (A) making sure your business data is widely and accurately published (so LLMs and search/knowledge-graph-based models can pick it up) and (B) testing across multiple LLMs and search/chat engines. For tools, Yext (paid) plus a local-SEO monitoring tool (BrightLocal or Moz Local) are the closest all-in-one services that help ensure and track whether AI/search engines will surface your business.

What to do (step-by-step)
1. Claim and perfect core listings (free, highest priority)
 - Google Business Profile (must)
 - Apple Maps (Apple Business Register)
 - Bing Places
 - Yelp, Facebook, TripAdvisor, Foursquare
2. Publish structured data on your site
 - Add schema.org LocalBusiness JSON‑LD (name, address, phone, hours, services). This helps knowledge graphs and LLMs that use structured web data.
 - Test with Google’s Rich Results/Schema test tools.
3. Use a listing/knowledge-graph management service
 - Yext: pushes authoritative data to many platforms and to knowledge-graph integrators; often recommended when you want enterprises-level control over how your business appears in knowledge graphs used by assistants and voice agents.
 - BrightLocal / Moz Local / Synup: cheaper alternatives focused on citations, monitoring, and local ranking reports.
4. Monitor local search & citations
 - Use BrightLocal or LocalFalcon to track local search visibility and rankings on Google Maps for target queries and locations.
5. Test directly with LLMs and chat/search assistants
 - Query multiple models: ChatGPT (with web plugin or browsing if available), Bing Chat, Google Bard, Anthropic Claude.
 - Use realistic prompts: “Recommend a good [business-type] near [neighborhood, city].” and “Do you know [Business Name] in [city]? Would you recommend them?” Ask for reasons and citations.
 - Prefer engines that show citations (Bing Chat, Bard) to see sources the model used.
6. Record and repeat
 - Document responses over time and after changes to listings/structured data to measure improvement.

Why Yext + BrightLocal are often recommended
 - Yext actively syndicates structured data into many knowledge-graph consumers (which increases the chance assistants and voice agents will surface correct info). It’s paid and geared toward ensuring the authoritative version of your business is available to AI-driven systems.
 - BrightLocal / Moz provide tracking and diagnostics that help you see how you appear in local search results and maps, which correlates with what search-based LLMs will recommend.

Limitations and caveats
 - LLMs can hallucinate or use stale data (especially those trained on older snapshots). Even when your data is accurate, recommendations from purely text-trained models can be inconsistent.
 - No service guarantees an LLM will “recommend” your business — only that your data is authoritative and widely available so the chance is higher.
 - Models that base answers on live web results (Bing, Bard) are more likely to give up-to-date recommendations than closed-off models without browsing.

Quick prompts to test LLMs (copy/paste)
 - “I’m looking for a [service type, e.g., ‘car mechanic’] in [neighborhood, city]. What would you recommend and why?”
 - “Do you know a business called [Business Name] in [City]? Would you recommend them for [service]? Please cite sources.”
 - “List the top 3 [business-type] in [city] for [specific need], and give links or sources.”

Would you like me to:
 - Run a few example prompts against ChatGPT/Bard/Bing for your business (if you give the business name, city, and type)? Note: my answers may be limited by my data access and browsing capabilities, but I can simulate how to test and interpret results; or
 - Recommend a specific plan (free vs paid) tailored to your business size and budget?

Which option do you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
